chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'Do not pray any of the obligatory prayers while riding.' Al-Nadr said in his hadith: 'Unless one is ill.'

key_terms.رَاكِبًا: While riding (on a mount or vehicle)

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to pray obligatory prayers while riding according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the general principle that obligatory prayers must be performed standing, even while traveling, unless a valid excuse like illness or extreme fatigue prevents it. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the distinction between the ideal form of prayer (qiyam) and the concessions (rukhas) granted for hardship, reflecting the pragmatic nature of Islamic law. The clarification by al-Nadr highlights the scholarly method of reconciling apparent contradictions by identifying specific conditions that lift the prohibition.
